title: Security & Pen Test Review - Acme Health
summary: Redwood and Acme Health reviewed the recent pen test findings for the hosted inference environment and discussed vulnerability management, secure SDLC controls, patching cadence, and encryption/KMS posture. Action items include sharing the redacted pen test report, providing network architecture and audit log retention details, and scheduling a follow-up to review remediation evidence.
action_items: Redwood (Elena) - Send redacted pen test report and remediation plan - 2025-03-07
Redwood (Ravi) - Share network architecture diagram and audit-log retention policy - 2025-03-06
Acme (Priya) - Provide list of critical assets and expected compliance timelines - 2025-03-10
Redwood (Jamie) - Schedule follow-up review to validate remediations and evidence - 2025-03-18
next_steps: Redwood to share redacted pen test PDF + executive summary
Customer to confirm SSO/SAML IdP attributes and SCIM provisioning requirements
Set up 30-min follow-up to validate patch evidence and SCA scan results
Provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation link
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-04 15:00 PT | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Morales (Redwood Security), Mark Stevens (CISO - Acme), Priya Kapoor (Sec Eng), Liam O'Neill (IT Ops), Sara Gomez (Privacy)

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, i'm jamie chen, i run the account for redwood inference. today elena and ravi are with me to walk through the pen test results and our vuln mgmt / patch cadence. mark, do you want to kick off?

[00:25] Mark: sure, thanks. we got the initial summary from your team last week. main ask is—what's the severity breakdown, what needs to be remediated for our audit, and how fast can we get fixes? we also need info for our SOC 2 scope and the dataplane residency questions.

[00:48] Ravi: yeah absolutely. quick caveat, the doc we sent is redacted for customer data. the full pen test PDF is internal but we'll share a redacted version for your legal team. high-level: there were no critical remote code execution findings against the hosted inference runtime. a couple medium findings—one misconfigured object store ACL in a staging bucket and one outdated nginx dependency on an infra instance used for metrics ingestion. a few low findings around info disclosure in headers.

[01:20] Priya: staging bucket ACL—was that user data? we can't have any PHI exposure.

[01:28] Elena: great question. that bucket contained logs and traces, not customer payloads; we confirmed no PHI. still unacceptable, we've marked it medium because of potential exposure. remediation is already applied for prod and staging, and we'll provide the S3 ACL change and proof in the remediation artifact.

[01:50] Liam: and the nginx one, is that on a customer-dedicated host or shared infra?

[01:56] Ravi: that's on a shared metrics worker in the hosted control plane—not in the inference GPU path. patched the package (CVEs: CVE-2024-xxxx) in the running image last week; rolling update completed. we'll provide the image digest and patch timeline.

[02:20] Mark: so that gives us comfort but for the SOC 2 auditor we need a timeline and evidence. what do you track for vulnerability management—SCA/SAST/DAST, SLAs?

[02:33] Elena: we have a formal vuln mgmt program: weekly SCA scans on images, daily vuln feed ingestion, SAST on PRs, and quarterly DAST on public endpoints. SLA tiers: critical (7 days emergency patch/hotfix), high (30 days), medium (90 days) by default, but we triage severity depending on exploitability. we also run monthly dependency-update windows for infra components.

[03:05] Priya: do you integrate tickets into Jira or other tracking so we can see evidence for the audit?

[03:11] Jamie: yes, we can provide a redacted Jira board export for the audit period; elena will attach the tickets mapping CVEs to remediation commits.

[03:22] Priya: good. next—secure SDLC, how do you enforce code reviews and secrets scanning?

[03:28] Ravi: PR gating is enforced—no merge without two approvers for service code, one for ancillary. we run Snyk/Trivy for SCA and a SAST tool in CI. secrets scanning with git hooks and pre-commit checks; any detected secret triggers an incident with forced rotation. we also do threat modeling quarterly for new features (especially anything touching customer data).

[03:56] Mark: what's your patch cadence for customer-facing infra vs control plane vs on-prem/private deployments?

[04:03] Elena: for hosted control plane and management plane components we do monthly patch windows plus emergency hotpatch for critical CVEs. For GPU inference nodes we are conservative—kernel and driver updates are scheduled quarterly with validated regression tests. For Dedicated / Private customers we offer configurable maintenance windows and can accelerate patches under contract.

[04:28] Sara: do you provide a mechanism for customers to opt into accelerated updates or block certain changes?

[04:33] Jamie: yes, Dedicated customers can set maintenance windows and choose immediate security-only updates. Private on-prem deployments are controlled by customer ops but we provide patch bundles and guidance.

[04:50] Priya: audit logs—what's retention, access controls, and do you push logs to customer SIEMs?

[04:58] Ravi: audit logs (control plane actions, API access, admin ops) are retained for 180 days by default for hosted but we have add-ons for longer retention. logs are immutable and signed; RBAC ensures only allowed roles can export. we support pushing logs via syslog/S3 or direct integrations to customer SIEMs (Splunk/Datadog). we'll share the retention table and sample log schema.

[05:28] Mark: encryption/KMS—where are keys stored, do you support customer-managed keys?

[05:34] Elena: we support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed KMS. for Hosted API we integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and support customer key provisioning via cross-account roles; for Private we support HSM integration. data at rest is AES-256; in transit TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred. we'll provide the KMS flow diagram for your security review.

[06:00] Priya: any reg findings about data residency? we need EU residency for certain datasets.

[06:06] Ravi: region-aware routing is available—we can pin inference workload to EU regions or Dedicated capacity in the region. we also have Private deployments for fully isolated residency.

[06:18] Mark: one auditor asked about RBAC and SSO—does Redwood support SAML/SCIM and fine-grained RBAC?

[06:25] Jamie: yes SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported, with role-based policies (admin, deployer, viewer) and per-route tokens. we also have audit trails for role changes. for enterprise we support custom roles via our console API.

[06:45] Priya: how do you prove least privilege—are API tokens scoped?

[06:49] Ravi: tokens are scoped to model routes, rate limits, and can be time-limited. we recommend short-lived tokens for automation and rotate keys routinely.

[07:00] Mark: ok sounds good. back to the pen test—any open items that remain outstanding?

[07:06] Elena: outstanding items were mostly administrative: confirmation of ACL remediation (done), providing image digests and patch timestamps (in progress), and a low finding on header hardening that we pushed a config change for. we estimate all medium items closed and we'll provide evidence.

[07:28] Liam: can you show the audit evidence flow—where will we find the logs and the proof that the S3 ACL was changed?

[07:34] Ravi: we will provide a conformed artifact set: cloudtrail entry for the ACL change, S3 bucket policy diff, the commit hash in the infra repo, and the container image digest. all redacted where needed.

[07:50] Priya: vulnerability scanning cadence—do you run container scans at build and periodically in runtime?

[07:56] Elena: yes, build-time SCA and daily ephemeral scans against running images; we also run weekly image rebase checks and automatic alerts if a new CVE crosses the high threshold.

[08:12] Mark: for the SOC 2 audit they asked for a list of third-party dependencies and vendor risk assessments—can you share a vendor inventory?

[08:20] Jamie: we can share a redacted vendor inventory and the attestation for third-party risk management. we'll include contracts for KMS providers and cloud provider attestations.

[08:34] Sara: data retention and deletion—how is customer data deleted on request?

[08:40] Ravi: we have APIs for data deletion and a documented retention policy; deletion requests are processed within the SLA in the contract—default 30 days for cached artifacts and immediate deletion for ephemeral logs in most flows. we'll include the deletion process doc.

[09:00] Mark: what's your incident response cadence and disclosure policy if a vulnerability is exploited?

[09:07] Elena: incident response team follows an IR runbook: containment, assessment, notification within our contractual breach timeline (48-72 hours for incidents with data exposure), and post-incident report with root cause and mitigations. we also have a responsible disclosure program and a security@ address.

[09:34] Priya: do you perform regular pen tests? frequency? and do you allow customer witnesses for tests?

[09:40] Ravi: third-party pen tests are annual at minimum; we also perform internal red-team exercises twice per year. for enterprise customers wanting a shared scope, we can coordinate a joint pen test or provide a tailored scope; customers can witness or request read-only evidence.

[10:00] Mark: one of our auditors wanted to know about change control for the inference models—how do you control model updates and rollbacks?

[10:08] Jamie: model rollouts are controlled via rollout policies in the console—canary, percentage-based, and immediate rollback if quality or latency regressions occur. we tie rollouts to CI/CD pipelines with immutable model versions and audit trails for who triggered a rollout.

[10:28] Priya: for patching cadence, if a critical CVE is found in a base image we spin emergency patch? what's your typical MTTR?

[10:35] Elena: for critical CVEs we aim for emergency patch within 48-72 hours including verification; for urgent customer-impacting issues we can coordinate an off-cycle maintenance window. mid/high we follow the SLA tiers I mentioned earlier.

[10:54] Mark: ok that matches what auditors expect. another ask: can you provide the control matrix mapping controls to SOC2 sections and ISO clauses?

[11:01] Jamie: yes we'll provide the controls matrix and mapping; elena will attach the SOC 2 Type II cover letter and the ISO attestation.

[11:15] Priya: log retention—you said 180 days default. is that tamper-evident and do you provide proof for auditors?

[11:22] Ravi: logs are write-once and we can provide signed digests and log snapshots. we also support exporting raw logs to your SIEM for independent retention.

[11:34] Sara: regarding KMS—if we supply our own key do you ever have access to plaintext?

[11:39] Elena: with customer-managed keys we do not have access to plaintext; the encryption/decryption happens in the customer-controlled KMS. we will document the key lifecycle, rotation policy, and access logs.

[11:56] Mark: anything in the pen test flagged as a repeat finding from prior tests?

[12:02] Ravi: no repeats. previous focus areas were cluster auth hardening which we addressed last quarter. this run had mostly one-time misconfigurations and dependency issues.

[12:12] Priya: curious about telemetry and debug endpoints—do you expose any debug endpoints that could leak tokens?

[12:18] Ravi: debug endpoints are behind RBAC and are not exposed to public. they require admin role and are audited. we will include the access control list for those endpoints.

[12:34] Liam: what's the remediation verification process? do you rescans after remediation?

[12:40] Elena: yes we run follow-up scans and request vendor pen testers to validate remediations for medium/high before closing tickets. we'll provide scan diffs and validation reports.

[12:56] Mark: excellent. operational question—do you provide patch notes and changelogs for each release?

[13:03] Jamie: yes release notes and security advisories are published; for Dedicated customers we can push a changelog to a private channel.

[13:18] Priya: remaining asks for the audit pack?

[13:22] Mark: redacted pen test, SOC2, ISO attestation, controls matrix, vendor inventory, KMS flow, audit log schema, proof of ACL and image patches, evidence of SAST/SCA results.

[13:36] Jamie: understood, we'll assemble the audit pack and send by EOD Friday next week.

[13:46] Elena: quick note on ransomware protections—we use immutable snapshots for logs and point-in-time backups, and we replicate backups to a separate account to reduce blast radius.

[14:06] Priya: curious about secrets management—do you recommend Vault or cloud KMS for customers?

[14:12] Ravi: we support integration with HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and GCP Secret Manager. we recommend Vault or CMKs for higher security posture.

[14:24] Mark: okay final wrap—can we get a date for the follow-up?

[14:28] Jamie: proposing 2025-03-18 for a 30-min remediation validation session. does that work for everyone?

[14:34] Priya: works for me.

[14:36] Mark: works.

[14:38] Jamie: great. quick recap: redwood to send redacted pen test + remediation evidence, SOC2 and ISO docs, network diag, KMS flow and audit log schema. customer to provide critical assets and any specific compliance timelines. follow-up scheduled for 2025-03-18. thanks everyone.

[14:55] End of call.

Notes: transcript includes some minor ASR errors (product names like "KV cache" sometimes noted as "K-V cache"), speaker attributions approximate in a couple places. Remediation ETA and evidence items agreed for the next steps.
